meta.storyTitle: Enable managed daemon lifecycle on macOS install

override.reason: User approved overriding the daemon review's unavailable browser rendering check. The reviewer verified the corrected LaunchAgent design in prose and found no new functional defect. The author independently rendered the sequence diagram in headless Chrome and verified the reservation, signed source, guarded rollback and terminal outcome labels.

summary.prose: Use a single signed source release tag. Compile at install time and retain exact local rollback bytes. Keep the supervised migration, crash recovery and existing command entry points.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

parameters.purpose: Private workspace, channel and trusted verifier inputs.

errors.condition: Required verification or lifecycle evidence fails.

preconditions: A trusted installer or installed verifier carries the pinned public key and authorized channel mapping. Fetch into an owner-private bare repository with controlled Git configuration and a trusted Git/SSH verifier.
postconditions: Require an annotated tag with a signed channel identifier and unambiguous version or sequence, a direct commit target matching the fetched release branch head, and an allowed signature. Verify before any candidate checkout, install script or bridge. Consume that immutable object through local staging.

Read the compatibility catalog as a bounded Git blob from the verified tree before checkout. The catalog keys predecessor declarations and launch profiles by exact prior commit. The signed tag target supplies the candidate commit identity. The installed controller validates the schema, graph and writable-format equality and explicit crash-consistent reopening eligibility. The catalog supplies the known declaration for a historical predecessor without one, and rejects a present conflicting declaration. Journal the verified tag and catalog blob IDs, ordered compatibility pair, approved launch profile and local byte pins for offline recovery.

api.name: completeLegacyMigration
api.signature: completeLegacyMigration(gate: InstallationMutationGate, update: UpdateReservation, pins: ManagedUpdatePins): Promise<DaemonUpdateOutcome>

parameters.name: gate
parameters.purpose: Owns the cutover and recovery reservation.

parameters.name: update
parameters.purpose: Identifies verified predecessor, release, fence and desired state.

parameters.name: pins
parameters.purpose: Carries the qualified prior and candidate releases.

returns.meaning: Verified committed cutover, verified rollback, or fenced recovery.

errors.condition: A release, launch route, exact exit, or recovery state cannot be verified.

preconditions: Use the migration-capable installer or updater to prepare the release before invoking any shutdown path. Freeze the canonical legacy launch and checkout paths and verify old mutating helpers are absent before cutover. Verify the pinned predecessor and public socket before sending shutdown.

For a later upgrade of a restored legacy generation, the trusted external entry point acquires an InstallationMutationGate update preparation reservation before fetching the bridge or candidate, running build commands or capturing local fingerprints. Under admission capture the authenticated restored process incarnation and running or stopped intent, then verify the same baseline immediately before cutover. Use the managed preparation reservation pattern. An admitted public stop wins if it reserved first and the updater returns busy. If preparation fails or is cancelled before mutation, record its failure and release the reservation after verifying the incumbent, selector and launcher are unchanged. Dead-owner recovery cancels preparation with no mutation or uses the journaled recovery path if cutover has begun. Upgrade admission stays held continuously when the qualified preparation becomes the cutover reservation.
Preserve exact prior launch route, selector, state and incarnation under admission.
postconditions: Preserve the original raw pin, job policy and stopped or running intent. Keep the canonical dispatcher fenced during candidate cleanup, selector reconciliation, predecessor launch and readiness verification, and until the rollback outcome and receipt are durable.

For a prior running install, the reservation owner alone may use the private, byte-pinned archived checkout. Reconstruct direct argv and cwd or a private launchd descriptor, mapping only pre-recorded checkout-contained executable/script/cwd paths from the captured inode to its archived location. Preserve UID, domain, label, argument order, runtime, state-root environment and RunAtLoad/KeepAlive policy. Verify the actual registered job and socket peer before recording readiness. A previously stopped job stays passive. Refuse ambiguous mapping and retain the fence.

Publish the terminal rollback outcome and verified legacy route together before enabling normal access. Keep a guarded canonical dispatcher after rollback. It can select the archived release only for the verified terminal receipt, route restart and update through the same gate, and support a later managed retry without releasing the old mutating scripts. Keep the archived location stable for the live job. Journal dispatch publication separately so interrupted settlement can reconcile without another spawn. Verify exact child or idle state and preserve a committed candidate without rollback.

Every restored running legacy route uses a trusted, byte-pinned rollback preload from the current installer/controller, passed as an explicit Node --import argument after scrubbing user injection options. For the supported predecessor the synchronous Node module hook matches the verified archived admin-handlers module URL and the pinned main/admin-worker importer URLs. It supplies wrappers for both sharedAdminHandlers and adminWorkerHandlers, retaining the original table except daemon.update and daemon.shutdown. The wrapper returns an update-via-current-installer refusal before invoking any old handler, so it never writes the old marker, spawns the old helper or schedules shutdown. The restored daemon keeps this refusal after terminal rollback and throughout any later migration attempt. The runtime and archived executable keep their raw pins. Set the launcher root to the stable guarded canonical dispatcher, while the daemon entry and cwd use the verified archive. Never resolve launcher operations through the archived checkout.

At startup require the preload and exact hook configuration in the main thread and any admin worker, including replacements. For the pinned old router, queued admin requests can only reach a constructed wrapped table. Profile validation proves the supported startup and worker imports, default worker argument inheritance and absence of an unguarded update route. A private preload receipt identifies the verified module and invocation for main and the admin worker. Fail startup or keep recovery fenced if the wrapper cannot attest either applicable path before readiness acceptance. Test both threaded and single-threaded operation. The original legacy IPC is unavailable for updating a restored predecessor. Current shell, TUI and IDE paths use the trusted installer route.

Both wrapped tables forward public daemon.shutdown to one process-level admission path. Before invoking the original drain, atomically acquire a stop reservation through InstallationMutationGate. A competing update, rollback, restart or stop reservation returns the existing busy response without entering the original shutdown handler. Hold an admitted stop reservation through exact predecessor exit and run-file reconciliation. The trusted controller records the generation and exact exit observer before admitting the drain and owns cleanup if the requester or old process exits. Recover abandoned admission through the existing journal and exact-incarnation evidence. A failed admission never schedules a delayed drain.

Give the admitted migration controller a private local drain channel furnished by the pinned adapter, independent of public daemon.shutdown. Use an owner-private socket with bounded, versioned messages and Darwin peer credentials. The adapter matches the controller peer UID, PID, start time and executable against the current durable reservation, and checks the operation, target state root, restored process incarnation and outstanding drain intent. Reject stale, repeated or mismatched requests without forwarding them. The controller verifies the adapter peer and arms the exact exit observer before sending the request. Main and worker public handlers share the same gate and cannot submit private drain authority. No caller can pass that authority as public RPC parameters.

Treat the private adapter's authenticated generation and both applicable handler receipts as prerequisites to publishing restored readiness. If the private endpoint or admission proof is missing, keep recovery fenced. During first migration from the untouched historical process, retain the existing authenticated legacy drain and exact-exit/rollback checks. Once restoration has installed the adapter, use the private route for every later controller drain. A stopped predecessor has no adapter process to drain.

For the known shell LaunchAgent only, replace its verified bash start wrapper with a controller-authored private launchd descriptor using the pinned Node executable, explicit guarded --import preload, original supported tsx loader, archived entry and cwd. Preserve label, UID, domain, approved environment and passive/RunAtLoad policy, pin both descriptor hashes, verify live registration and exact adapter/daemon peer before publishing rollback. A previously stopped job stays passive.

api.name: launchManagedUpdate
api.signature: launchManagedUpdate(entry: string, args: readonly string[], awaitReply: () => Promise<boolean>): Promise<{ launched: true; updateId: string }>

parameters.name: args
parameters.purpose: Carries the owned release and operation inputs.

parameters.name: awaitReply
parameters.purpose: Confirms that the update acknowledgement was written.

returns.meaning: Returns the admitted update identity while the helper owns completion.

errors.condition: Admission, trusted helper launch, or acknowledgement fails. Source verification or staging failure after acknowledgement is a detached terminal outcome.

preconditions: The already trusted installed helper reserves the update and returns its acknowledgement within the existing client deadline. Launch it without fetching, installing, building or inventory verification before the acknowledgement. Stopped updates use the local controller and preserve idle intent.
postconditions: Begin detached preparation only after confirmation that the acknowledgement was written. If reply delivery fails, cancel the unstarted reservation and leave the incumbent running. The helper verifies qualification and stages the candidate before any launcher fence, shutdown or selector change. A lost client connection after confirmed reply does not cancel the admitted update. Preserve the existing response shape and the test for preparation longer than both transport deadlines.

dataModelChanges.details: Persist one activation reservation per state root with exact owner, candidate and explicit start intent. Journal descriptor, provisional selector, exact registration, child admission, readiness and terminal outcome with identities. Previous journals remain decodable. Activation cleanup reverses only receipted owned mutations.

Persist a tagged managed, legacy-job, legacy-direct, or legacy-stopped predecessor. All variants bind canonical state root, prior release/runtime and candidate pin, selector baseline or absence, and prior running state. Managed carries supervisor generation. Legacy-job carries descriptor path/hash, verified label, UID, launchd domain, program argv, working directory and RunAtLoad policy. Running legacy-job and legacy-direct carry exact process incarnation, authenticated socket peer and pinned PID/socket identities. Legacy-direct also carries rollback argv, cwd and a release-qualified environment recipe reconstructed from the supported launcher, without persisting credentials. Legacy-stopped carries proof of no live process and either a pinned idle job or verified absence. Decode historical predecessor.legacy as legacy-job and older enabled prior without legacy as managed. Reject unknown or contradictory variants. Persist each observed exit, its drain classification, and ownership-fence evidence before candidate bootstrap. A rollback route maps only verified original checkout-relative argv/cwd paths into the archived directory. It binds a single archived release and recorded job or direct launch to the update and keeps the canonical launcher fenced until terminal evidence. The archive route pins one trusted preload, its supported old release and import/worker topology. The stable launcher root is distinct from the archived daemon cwd and entry. The old update RPC remains refused for this restoration generation. A restored incarnation owns one pinned adapter and one private drain endpoint. One stop or update reservation owns the matching drain authorization and exit receipt. An already-admitted public stop cannot overlap migration or rollback.

One signed annotated tag authorizes one channel and one commit. A reservation owns at most one verified source receipt and one pair of exact local pins. The receipt stores signer identity and tag, commit and tree object IDs. Keep a durable channel floor to reject replay of an older release and reuse of a sequence with a different tag. The candidate tree owns the bounded compatibility catalog, keyed by exact predecessor commit with explicit ordered-pair and launch-profile semantics. The receipt binds the catalog blob and decoded pair to the update for offline recovery.

Supersede published runtime references, Mach-O normalization and delegation metadata for new releases. Retain decoding needed for any historical journal already requiring offline recovery. No new authorization can use the prior unsigned route.

errorCases.scenario: An older launcher or updater can still mutate the legacy install
errorCases.detection: Resolve the canonical checkout and every supported launch route. Atomically exchange the canonical checkout entry with a gate-aware dispatcher on the same filesystem while the old daemon is still running. Preserve the displaced checkout separately. Before stopping, verify the dispatcher and archived checkout identities, an absent or owned legacy update marker, and absence of known old shell, detached helper and installer processes bound to the retired root, using verified argv and cwd. Repeat admission after the swap. An unrecognized launch path, unresolved process identity, live old mutator, or exchange failure makes exclusivity unproven.
errorCases.response: The dispatcher rejects concurrent mutation while cutover owns the reservation. Qualify only predecessors that acquire the shared run-file guard before opening data and whose shipped old commands use the canonical absolute entry. Keep that guard through owned cleanup and transfer it to candidate startup before the legacy route can reacquire it. Refuse when another legacy route cannot be fenced. Preserve or restore the old service before releasing a failed admission.
errorCases.userImpact: The supported update retries safely after a concurrent operation ends.

errorCases.scenario: Predecessor job or runtime does not match the qualified route
errorCases.detection: Match the verified launchd registration against its owned descriptor bytes and approved exact argv. Match direct socket peer and executable against the qualified launch recipe. Accept the documented recovery LaunchAgent only with its pinned tsx loader arguments, canonical entry, matching working directory, bounded owned descriptor and passive restart policy.
errorCases.response: Reject foreign jobs, unknown loaders or args, conflicting restart policy and unverifiable direct rollback settings before disruption. Recheck the descriptor, PID incarnation and run-file identities immediately before each action.
errorCases.userImpact: The updater reports the unsupported predecessor while preserving the current service.

errorCases.scenario: Exit is unconfirmed or graceful drain cannot be classified
errorCases.detection: Observe the exact predecessor exit independently of the broker and bind any qualified terminal evidence to the authenticated shutdown request and process incarnation. An RPC acknowledgement, socket close, PID disappearance, or generic log entry alone does not prove a graceful drain.
errorCases.response: Withhold candidate admission until exact exit is proved. Journal the exit plus graceful, broker-denied, or unknown. Use graceful only for a qualified positive completion signal, broker-denied only for correlated watchdog evidence, and unknown otherwise. Both broker-denied and unknown require a release pair explicitly qualified for crash-consistent reopening. Report the observed classification in the update detail.
errorCases.userImpact: The user can distinguish a verified shutdown from an exit whose drain could not be confirmed.

errorCases.scenario: Candidate bootstrap or readiness fails before a durable outcome
errorCases.detection: Registration, startup generation, owned run files, or candidate idle/readiness cannot be verified.
errorCases.response: Reconcile the candidate under the reservation, Keep the canonical dispatcher fenced while restoring the predecessor via the archived route. Publish verified rollback before enabling guarded ordinary commands. Retain a fence when restoration is unverified.
errorCases.userImpact: Verified rollback restores the previous service state and reports the failed update.

errorCases.scenario: Outcome publication throws or its acknowledgement is lost
errorCases.detection: Publication fails, or retry sees an active reservation without a verified terminal reply.
errorCases.response: Keep the reservation. Re-read the exact matching durable outcome through existing recovery. A durable success verifies or completes activation without rollback. A durable rollback verifies the old state. Only a proven uncommitted transaction can unwind. Unknown ownership remains fenced.
errorCases.userImpact: The updater reports an unconfirmed result until recovery determines the terminal state.

errorCases.scenario: A restored legacy client attempts an unadmitted lifecycle RPC or the rollback adapter cannot bind both handlers
errorCases.detection: The pinned adapter wraps both legacy admin factories and requires readiness receipts for each applicable path. Public shutdown requires a stop reservation. Private drain requires peer and intent checks against the current reservation and exact restored incarnation.
errorCases.response: Refuse public update and reject a busy public stop before the legacy handler can run. Accept an idle public stop through normal stop admission. A competing client or stale controller cannot initiate a private drain. Keep recovery fenced if adapter admission is unproven.
errorCases.userImpact: The previous service remains available through supported commands or the controller reports fenced recovery.

errorCases.scenario: Missing tag, wrong signer, channel, target, or stale sequence
errorCases.detection: Controlled Git verification and durable floor comparison.
errorCases.response: Refuse before checkout and npm. Leave predecessor service and selector untouched.

errorCases.scenario: Build, compatibility, raw-pin, or readiness verification fails
errorCases.detection: Check local build outputs, writable-format declarations, captured pins and supervisor readiness.
errorCases.response: Release an untouched preparation or restore the exact prior bytes and route after cutover. Keep fenced if recovery evidence is uncertain.

testStrategy.testFramework: Node test runner with real Git, disposable SSH signing keys, and macOS launchd integration. Retain Linux and IDE routing coverage. Acceptance criteria: ac1 Authorize the exact configured source before checkout. ac2 Pin and verify exact local rollback bytes. ac3 Preserve running or stopped intent across source-built migration. ac4 Keep restored lifecycle and retry guarded.

migration.stateBefore: Legacy or managed daemon installed from source. The reference-inventory implementation is development work.
migration.stateAfter: Authorized Git source builds locally and cuts over transactionally. Existing state and exact rollback bytes are retained.
migration.backwardCompat: Keep old journal decoding as needed for offline reconciliation. Existing users upgrade with the current installer or IDE. Fresh install and Linux remain within their existing lifecycle scope.

migrationSteps.action: Bundle the same trusted verifier and public key into the shell distribution and both IDEs.
Sign and publish the exact release head after source-built macOS tests. Publish tag and branch consistently and verify via the normal channel.
Reserve a restored route before slow work. Authenticate before checkout, stage the local build, and capture both raw fingerprints.
Verify and drain the exact incumbent. Activate the candidate under the supervisor or recover using the guarded original bytes. Publish the terminal result before releasing admission.

alternativesConsidered.name: Signed annotated channel tags
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Verify the exact locally built release source with Git.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Fetch privately, verify a signed annotated tag using an independently pinned release key, bind signed channel and commit, then check out its exact tree.
pros: One release signature and local compilation.
cons: Requires maintainers to sign each promoted source head.

alternativesConsidered.name: Signed commit plus separate channel policy
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Verify a release commit with the same pinned key.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Require a release-team-signed head commit and add channel metadata to signed commit content to disambiguate promotion.
cons: Couples ordinary source commits to release approval and branch metadata.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Applies release policy to source commits and complicates branch promotion.
